heading: Publication

calibration.sample: the 14 proofs of arXiv 0708.2185 (one category theory paper; a profile of that paper, not a general norm)
calibration.not_used: communicative function: annotators agreed on 34 of 50 sentences (connection against none), so no rule is derived from it

length_basis_rhgrh100.note: The 120/168 limits came from one paper whose own median proof is about 48 words; against this corpus they sit between the 41st and 53rd percentile, so they are kept.

sentence_sample_rhgrh100.sample: 60 proofs of 40-400 words, one per paper, from mark7rhgrh100-20260928; two annotators (codex-18, zai-2), same instrument as the one-paper profile
sentence_sample_rhgrh100.reading: PR1 holds on 60 papers: commentary-only sentences are about 1 percent of proof words or less for both annotators, and most of zai-2's in-flight labels are sentence fragments. PR3 holds: separate side-condition sentences are rare. The one-paper lemma-application share (32-42) is high for this corpus (about 25, wide spread). Section lead is not reliably measured: the annotators disagree on whether setup sentences count (per-proof correlation 0.01). About one proof in twelve opens with a one-sentence statement of method (by induction; following a cited argument), which PR2 as worded would forbid; no pilot telling uses one.

rules.rule: No sentence may be commentary only (placement inflight or leaf-section). A reason for a step may appear only as a clause of the sentence that takes the step.
No restatement of the claim before the derivation; the proof opens with the supposition.

The Schwarz equality case is cited by name in one sentence that lists the hypotheses it consumes; hypotheses are not checked in separate sentences unless the check is a computation the reader cannot be expected to supply.
At most 168 words; aim for 120 or fewer.
Every mandatory node of the content plan is realized or merged with an honest quote; every dependency between nodes in the alignment is still visible in the prose.
rules.from: programme gate for P3 and P4

nodes.reason: PR2; the closing sentence restates the claim.
The supposition is a step everything depends on.
Define g with its purpose as a clause (PR1).
The unit-disk bound is the one hypothesis check that is a computation; one clause or sentence.
PR3: cite the equality case, then specialize to g(w)=w.
Three steps: agreement on the disk, polynomial identity, top coefficient.

scaling-strategy.reason: Answered inside the step that defines g, as a purpose clause; no separate sentence.

rotation-specializes-to-identity.reason: The passage from the affine formula to g(w)=w is a derivation step, so it stays.

coefficient-extensionality.reason: Reading off the degree-N coefficient is a derivation step, so it stays.

schwarz-applicability-by-normalization.reason: Hypothesis checks are bundled into the sentence that applies the equality case.

schwarz-rigidity-connection.reason: The equality case is cited by name; its hypothesis inventory is not unpacked.

finite-domain-coefficient-boundary.reason: A boundary case is commentary; the sample proofs contain none.

fixed-point-applicability.reason: Bookkeeping over where g(0)=0 is used is commentary.

closed-disk-codomain.reason: Contested in the content plan; no support anchor.

dropping-fixed-point.reason: Contested in the content plan; no support anchor.

strategy-overview.reason: Contested in the content plan; the sample proofs have almost no lead-in.
